what_it_states: Model: the shuffle model extended to Private Individual Computation (PIC): each user applies a local epsilon-LDP randomizer to a bounded input (any two inputs of the domain are neighbours in the local guarantee), messages are encrypted with one-time public keys and shuffled; Theorem 5.1 (simulation security in the F_Shuffle-hybrid model, Appendix G) and Theorem 5.2 ((epsilon_c,delta)-DP by amplification via shuffling, Appendix H). Section 6: utility is the single-report error max_x E||R(x)-x||_2^2; for the l2 unit ball in R^d (and the l_infinity cube in Appendix A), Minkowski Response outputs a uniform point of the cap B_r(x) with the higher probability V(B_r)(e^eps-1)/(V(Y_r)+V(B_r)(e^eps-1)) and otherwise a uniform point of the r-expanded domain Y_r, followed by debiasing; r is set from the budget so that the error rate is of order (e^eps-1)^(-2/(d+2)) for large eps (Appendix A, equation 4: at most 24 (e^eps-1)^(-2/(d+2)) under its conditions). Theorem 6.1 (epsilon-LDP); Theorem 6.2 (any randomizer in the PIC model with fixed (epsilon_c,delta) has worst-case single-report MSE at least of order 1/n^(2/(d+2)) up to logarithmic factors; proof in Appendix I via a grid/transition-matrix argument and the shuffle-model DP constraint); Theorem 6.3 (Minkowski Response achieves O((log(1/delta)/(n epsilon_c^2))^(2/(d+2)))), hence asymptotic rate optimality in n. Section 7 and Appendices B-F: experiments on two-dimensional location data normalized to [-1,1]^2 (cap set with q=+infinity and a numerically searched radius), federated learning (d=4292), comparisons with Laplace, PlanarLaplace, Staircase, SquareWave, PrivUnit, PrivUnitG and PrivHS; Table 7 reports mean l2 errors of local epsilon-LDP randomizers on [-1,1]^2. The paper states the mechanism can be generalized to other Minkowski distances but treats the l2 and l_infinity cases.
what_it_does_not_state: No central additive-noise model with l1 (diamond) sensitivity; no translation-invariant planar noise law; no exact optimum or exact constant, only rates up to constants and logarithmic factors in the shuffle/PIC asymptotic regime; no all-law squared-Euclidean MSE optimum or selector for the planar diamond problem; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2 or its equality case; no rounded-core selector; no l1 cap/domain case is worked.
